Aim for Perfect, but be satisfied with Good Enough

It was brought up in the last link I mentioned, and repeated in a book I finished recently ( Difficult Mothers ): nobody can be perfect, but don't let perfect be the enemy of the good. That goes for everything: finding a man, cleaning, being a mother, whatever.

Do you want to settle for mediocrity? Because accepting a good enough effort is what that does. What you should always aim for is perfect and settling with your best effort which you don't have to be satisfied with. Hell you shouldn't be satisfied if there's still room for improvement. Try harder next time and settle for the maximum effort you can give that time too.

There is no achieving perfection. While there is nothing wrong with continuous improvement, it can become a problem if you are never satisfied with your current best effort. You need to let perfection go in the moment to enjoy life and be pleasant to be around.

If you keep baking cakes and then throwing them in the bin because the decorations are slightly wonky, who would want to live with you? You will never be happy with yourself either. If you burn the cake, sure, throw it out and start again, but if it is good enough, just eat it, enjoy it for what is good with it and learn from your mistakes for next time.

I combine a couple of my favorite principles for this. Compare yourself to who you were yesterday not who someone else is today & happiness is truly achieved when you understand that not all facets of your life will always be perfect. Happiness is choosing to be happy when most things are going well.
